hook.text: The riff that opens Ye Entrancemperium is taken from an unfinished Mayhem song, so Euronymous is credited in the liner notes.

facts.label: Recorded
facts.value: October to December 1996, Grieg Hall, Bergen, Norway

sentences.text: Compared with In the Nightside Eclipse, the lyrics shifted away from nature and Satanic themes toward mystical ones.
In 1996 the Reverence EP came out to tease this record, and it included the track The Loss and Curse of Reverence.
Because the riff comes from an unnamed Mayhem song, Euronymous, the Mayhem guitarist, gets a credit in the liner notes, even though he had died three years before this record was made.
The Mayhem bootleg Ha Elm Zalag holds a recording of that unfinished track.
The album was recorded from October to December 1996 at Grieg Hall in Bergen, Norway.
Eirik Hundvin, Ihsahn and Samoth are credited as producers, and Pytten handled engineering and production.
Ihsahn sang and played guitar and synthesizer, and he and Samoth both have arrangement credits.
Samoth played guitar, Alver played bass, and Trym played drums and percussion.
The playing is faster and more guitar-driven than on the band's previous album, with fewer keyboards, more clean singing and more blast-beat drumming.
In 1998 the record was remastered and reissued along with three tracks from the Reverence EP that were not on the album.
The band also made a promotional video for The Loss and Curse of Reverence, a track that appears on the EP and on the album.

listen_for.text: The opening guitar riff comes from an unnamed Mayhem song, and a recording of that unfinished track is on the bootleg Ha Elm Zalag.

listen_for.track: The Loss and Curse of Reverence
listen_for.text: It is also on the 1996 Reverence EP, the teaser for the album, and a promotional video was made for it.
It is an orchestral version of Inno a Satana, a different take on that song.
